business_goal: An HLS playlist and its segments register as ONE asset with a real, registry-native byte total; the registry is version-tagged (a pre-v2 registry is discarded wholesale and its orphans swept once); eviction removes the whole asset atomically without ever rescanning disk; every playlist/segment request always terminates with a response, exactly once, with an intact body (R2/R3/R6/R9/R10, A2/A3, UC-IngestHlsPlaylist + UC-IngestHlsSegment + UC-EvictCacheAsset, breadboard slices V2+V3). Extended in the round-4 device-smoke remap (2026-07-26) to own the request/response transport seam itself: BridgeServer.listen's httpServerResponseReceived dispatch (BUG-7 duplicate-listener double-dispatch) and HttpProxy.respond's error-body encoding (BUG-8 base64-mangled plain-text error bodies for WRITE_FAILED/ORIGIN_UNREACHABLE_NO_CACHE/SEGMENT_WRITE_FAILED/Bad Request) are both load-bearing for this same 'every request always terminates with a response' guarantee — ProxyCacheManager.ts (already this scope's substrate) is httpProxy.ts's sole production caller (`new BridgeServer(...)`, `this._bridgeServer.listen(...)`), and every error body BUG-8 corrupts is one this scope's own handlers (`reverseRes.send`) already emit.
